clue.text: Sense to bridge a river having heard Don sinks, perhaps

indicators.note: one word spans the other, so the first piece sits around the second

parts.note: sense in the meaning of sound mind, sanity

indicators.note: says the word for Don is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: to don clothes is to wear them

explanation.surface: Someone builds a bridge over a river after listening to a lecturer called Don.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don' is not a name or a lecturer but the verb, to put on clothes. 'perhaps' marks sinks as only one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathroom fittings such as basins and toilets are collectively called this, so sinks are an example.

clue.text: Bombshells, you are texted, force put aboard ship

indicators.note: being put aboard means going inside the ship's two letters

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the standard abbreviation for a ship
in text-message shorthand 'you are' is written UR
to prise something open is to force it

explanation.surface: A text message reports that a force has been put on board a ship with devastating news.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombshell is a shocking piece of news, an unexpected event.

clue.text: New talent show employee, not the first to be prompt

indicators.note: says the opening letter of the employee's title is dropped

parts.note: talent shows employ a panel member who gives verdicts on the acts, a judge

explanation.surface: A new member of staff on a television talent show is told to be punctual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prompt' reads as the adjective 'on time', but it is the verb, to give a gentle reminder.
explanation.definitionFit: To prompt someone is to remind or urge them, as with a gentle poke of the elbow.

clue.text: Whiff from tense people

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
a people, a nation or ethnic group, is a race

explanation.surface: Nervous people give off a whiff of anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: A whiff of something is a faint hint or slight amount of it, like a tiny residue.

clue.text: Northern town's alternative starter of haggis in batter

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'has': the northern town has the wordplay that follows

indicators.note: the other pieces go inside the word for batter

parts.note: to batter something is to ram it
an alternative is the other one

indicators.note: the first letter of the word haggis is taken

explanation.surface: A northern town offers its own version of a Scottish dish: haggis fried in batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like the coating for fried food, but here it is the verb to pound. ROTHERHAM is a town in South Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Yorkshire place is a town in the north of England.

clue.text: Engineer collecting missing base for carriage

indicators.note: the engineer's name gathers the other word up inside it

parts.note: James Watt was the Scottish engineer of steam-engine fame
something missing is gone
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: An engineer gathers up the parts of a carriage that has lost its base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as a verb but is a famous engineer, WATT, holding GONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagonette is a four-wheeled horse-drawn vehicle with facing side seats.

clue.text: Oppose republican even dropping by

indicators.note: says the letter for 'by' falls out of the word for even

parts.note: even, in the sense 'that even amount', means exact
the multiplication sign X is read 'by', as in a room three by four

explanation.surface: A Republican politician opposes something, even calling in to do so.
explanation.definitionFit: To react against something is to resist or push back on it.

clue.text: Having gathered pieces, dress is all there

indicators.note: the word for dress has the pieces gathered into it

parts.note: gardeners dress soil, treating it with compost
chess pieces are known as men
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collects the pieces of an outfit and pronounces the dress complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dress' is a gardening verb here, to treat soil, giving COMPOST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being of sound mind, fully in control of one's faculties, is colloquially being all there.

clue.text: Losing rag in road rage, criminal bearing blades

indicators.note: a criminal act is a crooked one, so the remaining letters are rearranged
losing says those three letters are taken out of the phrase road rage

explanation.surface: A driver in a fit of road rage loses a rag and turns criminal, carrying knives.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking RAG out of ROADRAGE leaves ROADE, which 'criminal' rearranges. 'blades' are not knives but the flat ends of oars.
explanation.definitionFit: A rowing boat fitted with oars, whose flat ends are called blades, is described this way.

clue.text: Slang for all to see reflected in a pub sign

indicators.note: the turned-round pieces go inside A and PH

parts.note: PH, public house, is the map abbreviation for a pub

indicators.note: a reflection shows the words mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: argot is a group's slang
U is the British film certificate for a film anyone may watch

explanation.surface: Slang words are displayed back to front on a pub sign for everyone to see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' is the verb, as in signing one's name. 'reflected' turns ARGOT and U into UTOGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: To put one's signature on something, for a fan say, is to sign it.

clue.text: Homeless dental hygienist working in indecisive manner

indicators.note: the remaining letters are put to work, shuffled into a new order
a home is a den, and 'less' takes those letters away from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A dental hygienist with nowhere to live goes about the job hesitantly.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DEN from DENTAL HYGIENIST leaves TALHYGIENIST, which 'working' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with hesitation, unsure what to do, is acting in an indecisive way.

clue.text: Soldier on a plain

parts.note: a, as in 'ten pounds a head', means per
a plain, unadorned style is severe

explanation.surface: A soldier is stationed on a stretch of flat country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier on' looks like a soldier standing on a plain; it is the phrasal verb meaning to keep going.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep going despite difficulty is to soldier on.

clue.text: Folding part of piano tested

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A folding piano is put through its paces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Folding' is slang for paper money, which folds in a wallet.
explanation.definitionFit: Folding money is banknotes, so 'folding' alone is slang for paper currency.

clue.text: Trapped inside school, a dumpy hairy creature

indicators.note: says the following pieces are caught inside the abbreviation for school

parts.note: short and thickset, dumpy, is squat

explanation.surface: A short, stocky, hairy animal has got itself shut inside a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigfoot, the legendary ape-like creature of North America, is covered in fur.

clue.text: Student experience mostly excellent

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to experience something is to undergo it
rad is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: Student life is described as largely brilliant.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone studying for a first university degree is an undergraduate, informally shortened.

clue.text: Vehicles offloading right skips for food stores

indicators.note: the vehicles unload, shedding the letter for right

parts.note: trucks are goods vehicles
to skip is to hop

explanation.surface: Delivery vehicles drop off their loads and leave skips at food stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skips' looks like rubbish containers but is the verb, hops. A TUCK SHOP is a school shop selling snacks, tuck being British slang for sweets and food.
explanation.definitionFit: These school snack shops are places selling and keeping sweets and food.

clue.text: Another newspaper job?

definitions.meaning: in the Telegraph, another paper is the Financial Times, written with its article
job is criminal slang for a robbery, as in an inside job

explanation.surface: Someone wonders about taking another post on a different paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer names the Financial Times, a rival to the Telegraph that printed this clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang a job is a robbery or burglary, a stealing of goods.

clue.text: Enlightenment from revolutionary Frenchman, author captivating you once

indicators.note: the turned-round names hold the old word for you inside them
in a down clue revolutionary means turned upside down, read in reverse

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name
Edgar Allan Poe was an American author
ye is the old form of you

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary and a writer enchant an old-fashioned audience with their enlightened ideas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses the Frenchman and author together, giving EOPENER, and 'captivating' takes the old word for you in after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A revelation, something that surprises and makes things clear, gives sudden understanding.

clue.text: Happy scratching place making you relieved

indicators.note: scratching out means crossing off those letters

parts.note: happy means pleased
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A contented creature finds a spot to scratch and feels relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Eased pain or worry has been lessened, leaving someone comforted.

clue.text: Fit rival? Not disheartened

parts.note: to rival someone is to compete with them

indicators.note: losing the heart, the middle letter, leaves only the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A fit sporting rival is not downhearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' sounds like physically fit, but means capable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fit for a task is able and qualified to do it.

clue.text: Lean back embracing a stunner

indicators.note: the turned word holds the letter A in its arms
back means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: to lean on something is to rest on it

explanation.surface: A slim, stunning beauty leans back into someone's embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stunner' suggests a beauty; it is a device that stuns, the electric weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: This electroshock weapon stuns its target, so it is literally a stunner.

clue.text: One trapped by distant relatives raised tone

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters read upwards, in reverse
the numeral is caught inside the word for the relatives

parts.note: apes are humans' distant evolutionary relatives
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Someone held captive by relatives from afar raises their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trapped by' puts I inside APES to give AIPES, which 'raised' turns around.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish-brown colouring, seen in old photographs, is a shade or tint.

clue.text: Clasp and wheel bearing breaking after almost year

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the word for wheel holds the rest inside it

parts.note: to wheel round is to spin

indicators.note: breaking up the letters rearranges them
almost means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A clasp and a wheel bearing break shortly after a year of use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wheel bearing' looks like a car part, but 'bearing' means carrying. The shortened 'after' is jumbled into AFET by 'breaking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent pin with a guarded point fastens fabric like a clip or brooch.

clue.text: Stench from feet, two are scrubbed intermittently

indicators.note: every other letter is wiped out, leaving the first, third, fifth and so on

explanation.surface: A smell rises from feet, and two of them are given a patchy scrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetor is a strong, offensive smell, a foul odour.

clue.text: Covertly approach area close to that upset dog

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read backwards
the close, or last letter, of the word that

parts.note: a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks up near an area where a dog is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football, to TAP UP a player is to approach them illegally about a transfer.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a secret, improper approach to a contracted player is called this in sport.

clue.text: Police officers frequently very forgiving

parts.note: supers is short for police superintendents
oft is an old word for often

explanation.surface: Police officers are often very lenient.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exceptionally soft is extremely lenient, easily excusing faults.

clue.text: Board transport, moving left to the end

indicators.note: moving says the letter changes place within the word
says where the shifted letter is put: at the end of the word

parts.note: a plane is a means of transport

explanation.surface: Someone boards a vehicle and moves the left-luggage to the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' looks like the verb, to get on transport; it is the noun, a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: A board of experts, judges or advisers sitting together is a panel.

clue.text: Cents, say, nerd nervously takes in outing for US tender

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the word for outing inside them
nervously says the letters are jittery, rearranged

parts.note: an outing is a trip

explanation.surface: A nervous nerd counts cents on an outing to buy a gift.
explanation.walkthrough: A CANDY-STRIPER is an American teenage hospital volunteer, named after the striped uniform. 'tender' is one who tends, not a bid or currency.
explanation.definitionFit: A US volunteer nurse's aide tends to patients in hospitals.
